title: Capability registry: every combination of the nine contract axes has one verdict, one rule or lane, and rendered tables

fixture.registry: torchfdtd/capabilities.py: AXES, RULES (ordered rejections with code path and exact message prefix), LANES (admitted entry points with code path and test), verdict(config)
fixture.scene_recipe: example_project(config): 2.4 x 2.4 um transverse, 2.4 um along the propagation axis, 0.1 um mesh, 3 PML cells (alpha 0), 12 steps, Yee sampling, a 0.45 um block (a straight guide for mode scenes), one source and one monitor set per axis value, boundary kind on the transverse faces of directional scenes; see the module docstring

reference_method: static inspection of the code: every rule's code path is imported and its source must contain the message it raises (pydantic literal messages are derived from the field's Literal); every lane's code path is imported; every 'unavailable' rule names a schema field or signature that the test inspects; the registry is evaluated over the full 211,680-combination product

observables.name: unused_entries
observables.definition: rules and lanes that no combination reaches

observables.name: rendered_files_current
observables.definition: docs/CAPABILITIES.md and torchfdtd/capabilities.json equal the renderer output

observables.name: api_serves_registry
observables.definition: /api/capabilities returns the Lumerical inventory plus a combinations block with kind capability_registry

acceptance.coverage: every combination of the product receives exactly one verdict; unused_entries == 0; admitted + rejected == 211680
acceptance.code_paths: every rule and lane code path resolves to a real module attribute; every non-unavailable rule's message fragments (placeholders removed) appear in that code's source
acceptance.source_of_limits: G2-03 specification: the registry states the valid combinations and the documents and UI tables are generated from it; no numeric threshold applies

notes: The registry describes project-declared scenes built by the recipe. The explicit node-tensor APIs also take FP64 tensors and PEC walls on projects that declare no tensor material; those diagnostics are noted on the rules, not represented as axis values. Declared at the base commit of the g2-registry branch; the implementation lands in the same commit series.
